rv.q: The story is so compelling, I highly recommend this production.
Man of the People has promise and needs an injection of backstory to flesh out some gaps and quicker pacing to shorten the run time.
This production of “Man of the People” gets us thinking about the role of medicine in our daily lives and the uses of science.

cn.t: Critics find this biographical play about 1920s medical charlatan Dr. John Brinkley an interesting true story hampered by uneven execution, with mixed reactions to its dramatization of the radio huckster's goat gland scam.
